traits.habitat_notes: Native to the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia and New Guinea; cultivated pantropically as a leaf vegetable and naturalised widely (south China, tropical Africa, the Americas). Best in full sun, hot humid lowlands below about 500 m.
traits.habit_notes: A soft, fleshy, mucilaginous twining vine climbing by its stems over supports; leaves thick and semi-succulent, older ones turning purple from the base; red-stemmed form 'Rubra' has red-purple stems and leaf veins. Flowers in thick axillary spikes barely open; fruits look like small dark berries full of violet juice.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a soft, fleshy twining vine with thick glossy ovate leaves and axillary spikes of small pink flowers and dark fruit.

host.note: Malabar spinach twines over hedges and fences a few metres high (Wikipedia, Flora of China: twining to several metres), so it climbs a 6-year oceanspray shrub, not the vine form's 30-year maple.
